raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Stacked on #47774 ("fla: Faster GDN chunk kernels for long prefill on gfx95"); this PR is the last two commits.

## Motivation

On MI355X the GDN chunk scan takes ~11% of a 100k-200k-token Qwen3.8-27B prefill (48 GDN layers). Per layer, for a
16384-token chunk: `chunk_h` 532-560 us, kkt + solve + w/u 356 us, the output kernel 199 us. `chunk_h` is the serial
recurrence: one program per (head, V block), 192 programs for 48 heads x 4, each walking 256 chunks one after the other.
It is latency-bound and most of the 256 CUs sit idle while it runs; the per-chunk kernels before and after it are
parallel over chunks but wait for it.

## Modifications

1. `SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE=1` (off by default): `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd` runs the scan of one sequence with at
   least 8192 tokens as up to 4 parts of whole chunks, at most one part per 4096 tokens.
   - The calling stream runs `chunk_h` part after part; the state passes from one part to the next through the pool slot
     in fp32, as it stays in fp32 registers within one launch.
   - A side stream runs the per-chunk kernels beside it: kkt + solve + w/u of part i + 1 and the output of part i - 1
     while `chunk_h` does part i. Events order the parts, and the calling stream waits for the side stream at the end.
   - The single pass stays for batches of several sequences, sequences under 8192 tokens, read-only states
     (`inplace_update=False`) and CUDA graph capture.
   - `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h` takes an optional buffer for the per-chunk states, so the parts write into one tensor
     of the full scan and callers that read the states (mamba state tracking) get the same tensor as before.
2. With the pipeline, the gate's chunk-local cumsum moves into the fused kkt + solve kernel
   (`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_intra(..., g_out=...)`): the kernel loads the chunk's 64 gate values anyway, takes
   `tl.cumsum` over them as `chunk_local_cumsum` does and stores it for the later kernels. Parts 1-3 then take their
   cumsum on the side stream, off `chunk_h`'s critical path. The one-pass path keeps `chunk_local_cumsum` (without the
   pipeline the fold does not pay: alone on one stream it costs about what the separate kernel did).

## Accuracy Tests

- Bit-identical by construction: the same kernels on the same per-chunk inputs (the [64] cumsum stays inside one wave64
  in both kernels).
- New unit tests in `test/registered/attention/test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py`: `test_pipelined_scan_is_bit_identical`
  (GQA 6:2; o, h and the state pool vs one pass at 16384 tokens / 4 parts, 12600 / 3 parts with a part boundary inside
  the last chunk, 8192 / 2 parts, 10000 tokens in 10240 rows with a padded tail; 8000 tokens, two sequences and a
  read-only state keep the single pass), and a cumsum test (with `g_out`, the cumsum, w, u and A equal
  `chunk_local_cumsum` followed by the current kernel, bit for bit, at 4096 and 4000 tokens and for three sequences).
  MI355X, this branch: 34 passed, 1 skipped, 19 subtests.
- Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 on MI355X with the variable on: greedy output ids identical to the run without it (4 prompts incl.
  100k-200k-token needle prompts), needle-in-a-haystack 30/30 at 100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.935-0.945 (0.925-0.950 on
  builds without it); a mixed soak (16 prompts of 100k-200k tokens next to 600 chat requests) serves every request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Qwen3.8-27B GDN shapes (48 heads, K = V = 128), one sequence, whole scan per layer (us):

| tokens | one pass | 2 parts | 3 parts | 4 parts | 4 parts + cumsum in kkt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 1159.6 | 1068.6 | 1021.9 | 975.6 (-15.9%) | -27.8 us more (-2.7%) |
| 12596 | 940.2 | 876.2 | 819.1 | 808.0 (-14.1%) | -11.4 us more (3 parts, -1.3%) |
| 8192 | 588.5 | 573.4 (-2.6%) | 569.0 | 640.3 | -4.7 us more (2 parts, -0.8%) |

The pipeline uses 4 parts from 16384 tokens, 3 from 12288 and 2 from 8192; below 8192 tokens the extra launches cost more
than the overlap gains (3444 tokens: 263 us in one pass, 329 us in 2 parts). Where the rest goes at 16384 tokens:
`chunk_h` alone takes 560 us and 710 us (+27%) with the per-chunk kernels beside it, which take 810 us instead of 563 us,
so even a perfect overlap ends at ~890 us. A higher stream priority for `chunk_h`, 5 or more parts, uneven parts, and
disjoint CU masks (`hipExtStreamCreateWithCUMask`; `chunk_h` still slows by 28%, so the contention is in the shared cache
and memory path) were all tried and are not faster.

End to end: Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), TP1 on one MI355X, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384
--page-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend aiter`; `python3 -m
sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-output-len 1
--max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 32 --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache`.

Commit 1, same GPU, runs in the order off / on / on / off, mean of the two runs per setting:

| prompt tokens | median TTFT off (s) | on (s) | change | mean TTFT change | input tok/s off | on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100000 | 2.560 | 2.498 | -62 ms (-2.41%) | -2.42% | 38,923 | 39,889 |
| 120000 | 3.222 | 3.155 | -67 ms (-2.08%) | -2.02% | 36,528 | 37,279 |
| 140000 | 3.939 | 3.859 | -80 ms (-2.03%) | -2.01% | 35,685 | 36,418 |
| 160000 | 4.740 | 4.660 | -80 ms (-1.69%) | -1.79% | 33,744 | 34,360 |
| 180000 | 5.538 | 5.444 | -94 ms (-1.69%) | -1.73% | 32,509 | 33,080 |
| 200000 | 6.457 | 6.354 | -103 ms (-1.59%) | -1.54% | 31,221 | 31,711 |

Both runs with the variable on are faster than both runs without it at every length.

Commit 2 (pipeline on, with and without the cumsum fold; before / after / after / before on one GPU or the mirror, five
GPUs, `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable`): median TTFT -0.19 to -0.37% (mean of 5 GPUs; -7 ms at 100k, -20 ms at
200k), input tok/s +0.21 to +0.32%, faster on every GPU at every length. Several long prompts at once (16 of 100k tokens
at concurrency 2 and 4, 8 of 200k at concurrency 4; three GPUs): median TTFT -0.06 to -0.32%, every request completed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Opt-in variable, documented in `environ.py`.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
Closing in favour of #47774, which now carries this PR's two commits as Part 2:

| commit here | now in #47774 | change |
|---|---|---|
| `b761f7b2db` | `75a99eed31` | Pipeline the GDN chunk scan of a long prefill over two streams |
| `a12543a057` | `7f85c4ce31` | Take the gate's chunk-local cumsum in the pipelined scan's kkt + solve kernel |

Reason: consolidation of stacked PRs by the same author, so the related changes are reviewed in one place. The code is unchanged: the commits were cherry-picked as they are (`git cherry-pick -x`, original message kept, plus a `Folded in from` line), and merging the consolidated branches gives a source tree byte-identical to merging the separate PRs (checked on the full Qwen3.8 MI355X PR stack). Description, accuracy and benchmark results moved with them into the new PR's body.

Please continue the review on #47774.

@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@
 from typing import Optional
 
 import torch
+import triton
 from einops import rearrange
 
 from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.chunk_delta_h import chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h
@@ -20,7 +21,9 @@
     autocast_custom_fwd,
     input_guard,
     is_intel,
+    tensor_cache,
 )
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 
 if is_intel:
     from sglang.srt.hardware_backend.xpu.kernels.fla.chunk_delta_h import (
@@ -31,6 +34,148 @@
     )
 
 CHUNK_SIZE = 64
+# Tokens per part of a pipelined scan (see chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_pipelined),
+# at most 4 parts; a sequence shorter than 2 parts runs in one pass.
+PIPELINE_PART_TOKENS = 4096
+PIPELINE_MAX_PARTS = 4
+
+_side_streams = {}
+
+
+@tensor_cache
+def _cu_seqlens_host(cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor) -> list:
+    return cu_seqlens.tolist()
+
+
+def _pipeline_plan(q, cu_seqlens, initial_state, initial_state_indices, inplace_update):
+    """(parts, sequence length) for a pipelined scan, or (0, 0) to run one pass.
+
+    Only a single sequence whose state goes through the pool in place qualifies:
+    the parts hand the state over through the pool slot. Not while a CUDA graph
+    is captured (the plan needs the length on the host).
+    """
+    if (
+        not envs.SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE.get()
+        or not q.is_cuda
+        or cu_seqlens is None
+        or cu_seqlens.numel() != 2
+        or initial_state is None
+        or initial_state_indices is None
+        or not inplace_update
+        or torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
+    ):
+        return 0, 0
+    seq_len = _cu_seqlens_host(cu_seqlens)[1]
+    parts = min(PIPELINE_MAX_PARTS, seq_len // PIPELINE_PART_TOKENS)
+    return (parts, seq_len) if parts >= 2 else (0, 0)
+
+
+def chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_pipelined(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    v: torch.Tensor,
+    g: torch.Tensor,
+    beta: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    initial_state: torch.Tensor,
+    initial_state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    seq_len: int,
+    parts: int,
+    output: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+):
+    """The chunk scan of one sequence (rows [0, seq_len) of the [1, T, ...]
+    inputs) as `parts` runs of whole chunks over two streams.
+
+    chunk_h is a serial recurrence over the chunks with a few programs per head
+    and leaves most CUs idle. The calling stream runs it part after part; the
+    state passes from one part to the next through the pool slot in fp32, as it
+    stays in fp32 registers within one launch. A side stream runs the per-chunk
+    kernels beside it: kkt + solve + w/u of part i + 1 and the output of part
+    i - 1 while chunk_h does part i. The kernels and their per-chunk inputs are
+    the same as in one pass, so the output, the per-chunk states and the final
+    state are bit-identical.
+    """
+    T = q.shape[1]
+    H, K, V = v.shape[-2], k.shape[-1], v.shape[-1]
+    if (
+        output is not None
+        and output.shape == v.shape
+        and output.dtype == v.dtype
+        and output.is_contiguous()
+    ):
+        o = output
+    else:
+        o = torch.empty_like(v)
+    if seq_len < T:
+        o[:, seq_len:].zero_()
+    nt = triton.cdiv(seq_len, CHUNK_SIZE)
+    cuts = [nt * i // parts * CHUNK_SIZE for i in range(parts)] + [seq_len]
+    # Each part's kkt + solve takes the chunk-local cumsum of its rows of g.
+    g_raw = g[:, :seq_len]
+    g = torch.empty_like(g_raw, dtype=torch.float32)
+    h = k.new_empty(1, nt, H, V, K)
+
+    def rows(x, i):
+        return x[:, cuts[i] : cuts[i + 1]]
+
+    def chunks(i):
+        return h[:, cuts[i] // CHUNK_SIZE : triton.cdiv(cuts[i + 1], CHUNK_SIZE)]
+
+    def intra(i):
+        w, u, _ = chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_intra(
+            k=rows(k, i),
+            v=rows(v, i),
+            g=rows(g_raw, i),
+            beta=rows(beta, i),
+            g_out=rows(g, i),
+        )
+        return w, u
+
+    def out(i, v_new):
+        chunk_fwd_o(
+            q=rows(q, i),
+            k=rows(k, i),
+            v=v_new,
+            h=chunks(i),
+            g=rows(g, i),
+            scale=scale,
+            output=rows(o, i),
+        )
+
+    main = torch.cuda.current_stream()
+    side = _side_streams.get(q.device)
+    if side is None:
+        side = _side_streams[q.device] = torch.cuda.Stream(device=q.device)
+    side.wait_stream(main)
+    wu = [intra(0)] + [None] * (parts - 1)
+    wu_done = [None] * parts
+    v_new = [None] * parts
+    h_done = [None] * parts
+    for i in range(parts):
+        with torch.cuda.stream(side):
+            if i + 1 < parts:
+                wu[i + 1] = intra(i + 1)
+                wu_done[i + 1] = side.record_event()
+            if i > 0:
+                side.wait_event(h_done[i - 1])
+                out(i - 1, v_new[i - 1])
+        if i > 0:
+            main.wait_event(wu_done[i])
+        w, u = wu[i]
+        _, v_new[i] = chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h(
+            k=rows(k, i),
+            w=w,
+            u=u,
+            g=rows(g, i),
+            initial_state=initial_state,
+            initial_state_indices=initial_state_indices,
+            inplace_update=True,
+            h=chunks(i),
+        )
+        h_done[i] = main.record_event()
+    out(parts - 1, v_new[parts - 1])
+    main.wait_stream(side)
+    return g, o, None, None, h, None
 
 
 def chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd(
@@ -45,7 +190,25 @@ def chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd(
     cu_seqlens: Optional[torch.LongTensor] = None,
     chunk_indices: torch.LongTensor | None = None,
     inplace_update: bool = True,
+    output: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
 ):
+    parts, seq_len = _pipeline_plan(
+        q, cu_seqlens, initial_state, initial_state_indices, inplace_update
+    )
+    if parts:
+        return chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_pipelined(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            g,
+            beta,
+            scale,
+            initial_state,
+            initial_state_indices,
+            seq_len,
+            parts,
+            output=output,

+            with self.subTest(label):
+                pool_init = (
+                    torch.randn(pool_size, H, V, K, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+                    * 0.1
+                )
+                cache_indices = torch.arange(
+                    1, len(lens) + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+                )
+                cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(
+                    [0] + torch.tensor(lens).cumsum(0).tolist(),
+                    dtype=torch.long,
+                    device=device,
+                )
+                q = torch.randn(1, T, Hg, K, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+                k = torch.randn(1, T, Hg, K, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+                v = torch.randn(1, T, H, V, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+                g = torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(
+                    torch.randn(1, T, H, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+                )
+                beta = torch.sigmoid(
+                    torch.randn(1, T, H, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+                )
+                results = []
+                for pipeline in (False, True):
+                    pool = pool_init.clone()
+                    output = torch.full_like(v, float("nan"))
+                    with envs.SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE.override(pipeline):
+                        o, _, h = chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+                            q=q,
+                            k=k,
+                            v=v,
+                            g=g,
+                            beta=beta,
+                            initial_state=pool,
+                            initial_state_indices=cache_indices,
+                            cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+                            head_first=False,
+                            use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+                            inplace_update=inplace_update,
+                            output=output,
+                        )
+                    self.assertEqual(o.data_ptr(), output.data_ptr())
+                    results.append((o, h, pool))
+                (o0, h0, pool0), (o1, h1, pool1) = results
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(o1, o0))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(h1, h0))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(pool1, pool0))
+                if sum(lens) < T:
+                    self.assertTrue(
+                        torch.equal(
+                            o1[:, sum(lens) :], torch.zeros_like(o1[:, sum(lens) :])
+                        )
+                    )
+
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+    # The fused kkt + solve kernel writes all of A (no zero fill first)
+    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    def test_intra_writes_every_element_of_a(self):
+        """A is allocated without a fill, so the kernel must write every element
+        of each chunk's rows, including the zero blocks above the diagonal.
+
+        Runs the intra-chunk forward with fresh memory holding 0 (what a zero
+        fill gave), NaN and 7, and expects the same bits from all three.
+        """
+        device = get_device()
+        if device == "xpu":
+            self.skipTest("XPU runs its own chunk_fwd kernels")
+        dtype = torch.bfloat16
+        H, Hg, K, V, BT = 6, 2, 128, 128, 64
+        empty = torch.empty
+
+        for label, lens in (("one sequence", [300]), ("varlen", [64, 1, 130, 77])):
+            with self.subTest(label):
+                torch.manual_seed(0)
+                T = sum(lens)
+                cu_seqlens = None
+                if len(lens) > 1:
+                    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(
+                        [0, *itertools.accumulate(lens)],
+                        dtype=torch.long,
+                        device=device,
+                    )
+                k = torch.nn.functional.normalize(
+                    torch.randn(1, T, Hg, K, device=device), dim=-1
+                ).to(dtype)
+                v = torch.randn(1, T, H, V, dtype=dtype, device=device)
+                g = chunk_local_cumsum(
+                    torch.nn.functional.logsigmoid(torch.randn(1, T, H, device=device)),
+                    chunk_size=BT,
+                    cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+                )
+                beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(1, T, H, device=device)).to(dtype)
+
+                runs = []
+                for fill in (0.0, float("nan"), 7.0):
+
+                    def stale_empty(*args, fill=fill, **kwargs):
+                        out = empty(*args, **kwargs)
+                        return out.fill_(fill) if out.is_floating_point() else out
+
+                    with mock.patch.object(torch, "empty", stale_empty):
+                        runs.append(
+                            chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_intra(
+                                k=k, v=v, g=g, beta=beta, cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens
+                            )
+                        )
+
+                w0, u0, A0 = runs[0]
+                upper = torch.ones(BT, BT, dtype=torch.bool, device=device).triu(1)
+                for fill, (w, u, A) in zip(("nan", "7"), runs[1:]):
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(A, A0), f"A differs with {fill}")
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(w, w0), f"w differs with {fill}")
+                    self.assertTrue(torch.equal(u, u0), f"u differs with {fill}")
+                # Within each chunk, entries above the diagonal stay zero.
+                starts = [0, *itertools.accumulate(lens)][:-1]
+                for start, n in zip(starts, lens):
+                    for c in range(0, n, BT):
+                        rows = min(BT, n - c)
+                        block = A0[0, start + c : start + c + rows].transpose(0, 1)
+                        self.assertFalse(block[:, upper[:rows]].any())
+
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

Closing in favour of #47774, which now carries this PR's two commits as Part 2:

| commit here | now in #47774 | change |
|---|---|---|
| `b761f7b2db` | `75a99eed31` | Pipeline the GDN chunk scan of a long prefill over two streams |
| `a12543a057` | `7f85c4ce31` | Take the gate's chunk-local cumsum in the pipelined scan's kkt + solve kernel |

Reason: consolidation of stacked PRs by the same author, so the related changes are reviewed in one place. The code is unchanged: the commits were cherry-picked as they are (`git cherry-pick -x`, original message kept, plus a `Folded in from` line), and merging the consolidated branches gives a source tree byte-identical to merging the separate PRs (checked on the full Qwen3.8 MI355X PR stack). Description, accuracy and benchmark results moved with them into the new PR's body.

Please continue the review on #47774.
